title: Fodor's Pressing-Down Lemma for Regular Uncountable Cardinals
description: Formalizes Fodor's pressing-down lemma: for any regular uncountable cardinal κ, any regressive function on a stationary set S ⊆ κ.ord is constant on some stationary subset. Builds infrastructure not in Mathlib: IsClubBelow, diagInter with both parts proved. 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Fodor (1956) proved the pressing-down lemma, fundamental to set-theoretic combinatorics. A function f: S → κ is regressive if f(γ) < γ for all γ > 0. The lemma says such functions are 'eventually constant' on any stationary set.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Fodor's pressing-down lemma: any regressive function on a stationary set S ⊆ κ.ord (κ regular uncountable) is constant on some stationary subset of S.
overview.proofStrategy: Diagonal intersection: Δ_{β<κ}(f β) = {γ < κ | ∀ β < γ, γ ∈ f β} is a club when each f β is a club (two parts: closed = diagInter_isClosedBelow, unbounded = diagInter_isUnboundedBelow via zipper). Fodor: suppose not — pick clubs C_α avoiding fiber α. Diagonal intersection D meets S at some γ. But then γ ∈ C_{f(γ)} by regressiveness — contradiction.
keyInsights: **Diagonal intersection lemma**: Δ(f β) is a club when each f β is a club — the unbounded part requires a 'zipper' construction to find arbitrarily large points in the intersection.
**Stationary-club intersection**: every stationary set meets every club (definition of stationarity) — this is the key interface between the two worlds.
**New infrastructure**: IsUnboundedBelow, IsClubBelow, IsStationaryBelow are defined fresh as Mathlib (2026-04) lacked them.

sections.title: Fodor's Lemma via Diagonal Intersection
sections.summary: IsUnboundedBelow, IsClubBelow, IsStationaryBelow. diagInter. diagInter_isClosedBelow, diagInter_isUnboundedBelow. fodor: regressive → constant on stationary subset.
sections.mathContext: Regressive $f: S \to \kappa$ on stationary $S \subseteq \kappa$: $\exists$ stationary $T \subseteq S$, $f\restriction_T$ constant.

conclusion.summary: 15 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Fodor's pressing-down lemma proved with complete diagonal intersection infrastructure.
conclusion.implications: Fodor's lemma is a key tool in set theory with applications in combinatorial set theory, infinite graph theory, and forcing arguments.
openQuestions: Can Fodor's lemma be contributed to Mathlib?
Can the club filter on a regular cardinal be formalized?
Can Silver's theorem (SCH fails at singular strong limit) be derived using Fodor?
